label: rem:archimedean-realization-functor-interpretation
title: Archimedean realization: functor vs. motivic measure and identification with $\tau$
html:
Realization and projection. A motivic integral \int_{\mathcal{L}(X)} d\mu \in \widehat{\mathcal{M}} defines a geometric shape. The topological realization \chi_{\mathrm{top}} maps this shape to an integer (Euler characteristic) or a refined Hodge-theoretic invariant like hyperbolic volume. The adelic projection \pi_\infty discards non-archimedean components, returning the real-valued laboratory measurement.

Level of the construction (functor vs. motivic measure). As written, \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}} has domain the Grothendieck ring \widehat{\mathcal{M}} = K_0(\mathrm{Var})^{\wedge}, and \chi_{\mathrm{top}} \colon K_0(\mathrm{Var}) \to \mathbb{Z} is a ring homomorphism — a motivic measure in the sense of Denef–Loeser — while \pi_\infty is an archimedean place. A map out of a ring is not a functor between categories: "functor" is literally accurate only for the fibre functor \tau (below), or when the domain is lifted to the category of motives \mathrm{DM}(k), where Betti/Hodge realization is a bona fide functor. On \widehat{\mathcal{M}} itself, \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}} is the archimedean realization / evaluation into \mathbb{R}, not a functor between QOU categories — consistent with the notation register, which reserves "functor" for \tau and treats the R \mapsto \mathbb{R} realization as an evaluation. The block label is retained for stability.

Identification with the fibre functor. The QOU fibre functor \tau \colon \mathbf{C} \to \mathbf{Arch} is the exclusive exit from the categorical substrate to the real numbers. On motivic QOU inputs, \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}} coincides exactly with the archimedean component of \tau:

  \mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{top}}
  \;=\;
  \tau_{\mathrm{arch}}
  \;:=\;
  \pi_\infty \circ \tau
  \quad\text{on } \widehat{\mathcal{M}}_{\mathrm{QOU}}
  \;\subseteq\; \widehat{\mathcal{M}}.

Synthesis. The framework processes discrete categorical data along a single chain: adelic stitching, motivic integration, and archimedean projection. It requires no continuous differential equations or Lebesgue measures. The Kashaev limit of the algebraic quantum volume exemplifies this mechanism.
